record.context_brief: Reality of zeros for Wright functions fm
record.original_question:
For a nonnegative integer m, define f_m(x) = Σ_{k≥0} Γ(mk+1) x^k /
(Γ((m+1)k+1) k!). It is known that f_0(x)=J_0(2√x)
and f_1(x)=cosh(√x) have only real zeros. Determine whether f_m(x) has
only real zeros for every integer m ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each nonnegative integer $m$, define the entire function
$$f_m(x) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\Gamma(mk+1)}{\Gamma((m+1)k+1)\, k!}\, x^k.$$
One checks that $f_0(x) = J_0(2\sqrt{x})$ (a Bessel function) and $f_1(x) = \cosh(\sqrt{x})$, and in both cases all zeros of $f_m$ are real. Determine whether, for every integer $m \ge 2$, the entire function $f_m(x)$ has only real zeros.
artifact.category_tag: Reality of zeros of entire functions
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search located general results on the asymptotic distribution and reality of zeros of Wright-type entire functions, but none of the located sources specifically resolves whether the particular sequence $f_m(x)$ with coefficients $\Gamma(mk+1)/(\Gamma((m+1)k+1)k!)$ has only real zeros for all integers $m \ge 2$. No published resolution of this particular reality-of-zeros question was found.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics of Zeros of the Wright Function
status_evidence.snippet: For ρ > 0 all zeros with large enough index are simple and lie on the negative real semi-axis; for -1/3 ≤ ρ < 0 all zeros with large enough index lie on the positive real semi-axis.
status_evidence.claim: General asymptotic results exist on the location of zeros of Wright functions, but they describe only sufficiently large zeros and do not settle reality of all zeros of f_m for m ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: The Wright function and its applications
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of analytic properties, asymptotics and zero distribution of the Wright function.
status_evidence.claim: No specific resolution of reality of zeros of f_m for general m ≥ 2 is reported in available surveys.
